summary: Part of Garphill Games' West Kingdom trilogy, Paladins has players recruiting workers to build city districts, defend against raiders, and spread faith, with a shared threat track that everyone contributes to and benefits from. It's a mid-heavy worker placement game with a satisfying tableau of building cards and dual-use resources.
praised: Great worker-placement puzzle with meaningful choices each turn
Attractive production and thematic building cards
criticised: Similar feel to its sister games (Architects, Viscounts) can feel repetitive if you own multiple
Some rules overhead with commissions and virtue track

interaction.kind: paying opponents to reuse their occupied worker-placement spots
interaction.detail: Instead of spots being fully blocked, a player can place on an action space an opponent already occupies by paying that opponent a resource, so turn order and space choice have a direct financial effect on others. Outside of that toll mechanic and some shared market/track competition, each player mostly develops their own tableau and city defenses.
interaction.said: Reviewers of the West Kingdom trilogy commonly note it's 'friendly worker placement' — 'you can place on a spot someone else already used, you just pay them a fee,' which is called out as a distinctive, comparatively gentle form of interaction.

subsystems: city building (tile placement for VP and set bonuses)
sources: faith bonus / corruption penalty at game end
scoring.how_you_win: Place workers to build fortifications, recruit paladins, and fight off invaders while managing faith against corruption; highest total score when the final round ends wins.
